findings.problem: Base and restored matching accept a nominal timestamp inside the interval even when its declared uncertainty crosses the interval. This contradicts exact bound interval membership and makes a request/event look established at a time it may not have occurred. The profile matcher already applies conservative clock bounds.
findings.proposedRepair: Make base/restored matching assess explicit finite source clock uncertainty and require the full clock interval to lie inside the original interval for yes; crossing or unavailable bounds remain unknown. Specify that rule in public matching criteria, not only profile code.
findings.scenario: APP-CX-01: timestamp 10:00:01 ±120 seconds against [10:00,11:00) currently matches yes.

findings.problem: Base/restored matching picks the first matching record, so multiple lifecycle records for one request can yield incompatible classification based only on list order. A queued/requested/accepted observation must not stand in for execution or delivery, nor hide a later completed observation.
findings.proposedRepair: Require an explicit unique selectedRecordId when multiple records match, or a separately defined lifecycle aggregation with ordering, phase/outcome evidence and contradictions retained. Keep request handling, attempts, acceptance, execution and delivery as distinct propositions and required discriminators. Reuse the profile selection discipline in the base/restored contract.
findings.scenario: APP-CX-02: queued/executed records for the same application/request flip the executed-phase hypothesis from no to yes when only list order is reversed.

findings.problem: All factual downstream work requires a supported named technical hypothesis, and the sole validation continuation is hypothesis testing. An open/refuted explanation blocks independently evidenced scope, relations, technical sources, measured effects and later cross-domain discovery. Unknown hypothesis or scope is then sent to the base Q601 predicate that characterizes the validated request-handling event itself as unresolved.
findings.proposedRepair: Preserve optional named-hypothesis routes, while allowing separately evidenced factual scope, relationships, source and effects without a supported explanatory hypothesis. Carry per-proposition unknowns/refutations and add qualified retention endings for validated facts with open explanations. Change Q601 and its rule to retain the actual unresolved prerequisite/assessment while preserving known event answers, as qualified profiles already do.
findings.scenario: APP-CX-03: Q6=yes, Q85=yes, no explanatory hypothesis → Q190=unknown and Q601=yes. APP-CX-05 supplies a complete bounded source inclusion and comparable queued-action-count metric yet Q279/Q509 are both blocked first by the missing hypothesis.

findings.problem: Restored unprofiled routes often retain a different evidence facet from the source. A routeBasis note says the unrelated terminal focus may be recorded open, but introduces an unmotivated question and does not make the actual endpoint predicate follow from the source inquiry.
findings.proposedRepair: Give base retention endpoints neutral predicates that retain the actual source focus and its open questions, or add an explicit facet-preserving adapter with no invented assessment. The qualified profile terminal predicates provide an existing neutral pattern.
findings.scenario: Q62-no-Q536 changes execution-lineage inquiry to transport-metadata retention; Q127-no-Q569 changes API provenance to transport metadata; Q485-yes-Q543 changes API metric inquiry to control-plane retention. None of these decisions itself creates that new question.

findings.problem: Relation endpoint evaluation silently sets the target interval to the source interval. The public binding rule permits each relation to name its own target subject/time context, but delayed/serial observations outside the original source interval cannot be assessed without expanding or rebinding the source.
findings.proposedRepair: Require and preserve targetInterval separately when assessing a named target; validate each endpoint inside its own clock-bounded interval. Use an explicitly stated common comparison window only for predicates that require one. Never silently widen or overwrite the source context.
findings.scenario: APP-CX-06: a queued source action at 10:30 and separately originating next action at 11:30 share a typed assessed sequence identifier with explicit source [10,11) and target [11,12) bounds. The target is nevertheless rejected by source-interval substitution.

findings.problem: Qualified profile definitions are published over the branching graph, but the shown profile route evaluator selects retained same-domain continuations and rejects a domain crossing. Cross-domain readiness metadata instead requires base target fields and has no target profile/version handling. This demonstrates base discovery leads and same-domain profile assessment separately, not qualified profile-to-profile cross-domain traversal.
findings.proposedRepair: Document that exact evidence boundary. If qualified cross-domain traversal is intended, make target definition/profile/version and profile-specific binding fields explicit in selection/readiness, preserving source profile and independently qualified target contexts. Add independent agent-action→host-state and session-state→identity-state lead cases before claiming that integration.
findings.scenario: An agent execution-lineage observation discovers a named host-state observation with hostId/stateKey but no processId. A qualified host-state question can assess it; the existing base Q2 lead readiness still requires hostId/processId and the profile route evaluator cannot cross domains.

positiveFindings: Public nodes assess technical evidence and contain no vendor command/API implementation, action authority, approval or business-policy logic. Observed agent/tool facts remain legitimate public evidence questions.

New cross-domain leads preserve source answers, require independent discovery and complete target context, allow no/unknown source answers, and infer no target answer. The base lead contracts are semantically defensible within their explicitly narrow event definitions.
Optional corroboration, dependency, relation and technical-source negatives/unknowns generally continue without suppressing later measured effects.
Application state/session/agent profiles correctly avoid fabricated request IDs; phase-specific agent outcome discrimination passes APP-CX-04.
Qualified profile terminal predicates use neutral retention and unresolved-prerequisite wording that improve the base endpoint semantics.
